per_view.notes: RENDER-A and RENDER-B are visually indistinguishable at this camera: same geometry, colors, seams, gear and hump. Both share stepped fuselage segments, a blister-like hump, and only two clearly separated nacelles visible.

RENDER-A and RENDER-B are visually indistinguishable at this camera: same geometry, same navy-on-white livery, same fuselage step seam, same gear cluster. Both share a too-short bulbous hump and a thin high tail boom versus the photos.

RENDER-A and RENDER-B appear pixel-identical from this head-on camera: same geometry, livery, gear cluster and fin. No criterion distinguishes them; both show the horizontal stabilizer as a thin unswept slab.

The two renders are pixel-indistinguishable from this rear camera. Both share the same shortfalls versus the photos: no upper-deck hump shoulder, an unswept slab fin, untapered wings, and an all-grey livery instead of white-over-grey.

RENDER-A and RENDER-B are pixel-indistinguishable from this top-down camera. Both show a slender white fuselage, four underwing nacelles, swept tapering wings and a navy-edged fin; neither matches the reference's wider inboard-engine spacing or wingtip extension.
RENDER-A and RENDER-B appear pixel-identical from this camera: same geometry, livery, gear and shading. Both share one deficit versus the photos — the upper-deck hump is far too shallow.
